name: WV-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+20 district partisan lean in deep-red West Virginia
Incumbent Riley Moore with 10x fundraising advantage
No polls or expert ratings; challenger underfunded
model.rationale: The R+20 baseline, Moore's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and Polymarket's 97% Republican pricing all point the same direction, with no evidence of Democratic strength. I hold essentially at the baseline with a slight money-driven nudge.
model.watch: A late surge in outside spending against Moore or a polling error of historic magnitude would be needed to move this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Virginia's 2nd District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly R+20. First-term incumbent Riley Moore is running for reelection and holds a commanding financial position, having raised over $1.3 million with about $750,000 on hand. His Democratic challenger, Ace Parsi, has raised about $134,000 with limited cash remaining, and no outside spending has materialized on either side.

There are no public polls or expert ratings for this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which give the Democrat roughly a 3% chance. The baseline model points to a Republican margin near 18 points, consistent with the district's lean and the incumbent's advantages. Barring an extraordinary shift, Moore is heavily favored to win reelection.
